arguments.text: An assertion function that returns TRUE when the assertion is met and FALSE otherwise.

arguments.name: value
arguments.text: A function with parameters call and env that returns the message as a string.

origin.details: Stores the handler on the assertion. The handler's formals must be exactly call and env. see_if calls it with the matched call and the evaluation environment.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: An assertion function that returns True when the assertion is met and False otherwise.

arguments.name: value
arguments.text: A function with parameters call and env that returns the message as a string.

translation.details: Python has no replacement functions, so this is set_on_failure. The handler's parameter names must be exactly call and env. see_if calls it with the matched call and the evaluation environment.
translation.example:
from assertthat import assert_that, see_if, set_on_failure
from assertthat.expr import render


def is_odd(x):
    assert_that("is.numeric(x)", "length(x) == 1")
    return x % 2 == 1


print(see_if("is_odd(2)"))


def fail(call, env):
    return render(call["x"]) + " is even"


set_on_failure(is_odd, fail)
print(see_if("is_odd(2)"))
